record_notes.DCP-LETT-1229A: February 25, supplied 1849 from postmark. Full original manuscript transcription replaces earlier catalogue text. Replies to missing Simmonds letter, explicitly limited New Bay experience and no Chubut visit; water, brush, coal, fish and interior knowledge qualified. Patagonia and Falklands settlement recommendations, racial and colonial judgments are historical Darwin voice, not present recommendations or verified facts. Two unlucky-weather visits do not establish universal climate; later wheat reports uncertain. Health limits reply, not evidence of incoming receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1217: Friday assigned February 16, 1849 from mourning paper and February 22 answered endorsement; retain editorial assignment rather than treating dateline as explicit full date. Requests South American geology sales net commission to offset private account, without asserting sales occurred or knowing totals. Coral and volcanic volumes queried from curiosity, no financial interest. February 25 payment recorded later, not present account. Missing publisher account and February 22 reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13843: January 9, supplied 1850. Full clear Sowerby Jr note and drawings safely returned, exact arrival unknown. June timing accepted; fat and lean discussion and added text concern work in progress. Lithograph circular apparently used as envelope; blank receipts and subscriber list expressly not received. June 24 payment and completed publications are later evidence, not present result. Missing incoming note cannot be reconstructed from thanks.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1249F: August 9, supplied 1849 from later Lyell dinner account. Third-person Mr Darwin followed by first-person Charles Darwin signature remains one author. Accepts Lady Mahon invitation for Thursday; footnote chooses August 16 but August 9 was itself Thursday, so precise dinner day is not independently established by this note. Acceptance is not attendance. Missing invitation and later September report separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1050A: January 2, supplied 1847. Both volumes of Stokes Discoveries received yesterday, January 1 under assigned year, not proof fully read. January 16 Saturday invitation and train/fly logistics prospective; expected naturalists not confirmed attendance. Earlier congratulations and Grey controversy do not prove delivery or supply this missing cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1263: Book and stationery order, on or before October 24, 1849, with raw XML latest October 23 and uninformative 1809 lower bound. Inclusive human label conflicts with encoded exclusive latest; no exact day chosen. Raw body literally contains diag, dashes and ramme, without diagram node or recoverable layout alternative; do not silently repair. Humboldt book is Karl Wilhelm, not Alexander. Six cards of specified pens and 100 newspaper covers are orders, not receipts. Miller reading November 21, 1849 and Humboldt partial reading April 20, 1852 are later, not order-date knowledge. Wednesday-night delivery and Thursday carrier prospective; recipient conjectured.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1062: Henry Allen Wedgwood incoming cover dated February 21, 1847 plus copied proposal internally dated February 22. Distinguish Henry Allen author from Hensleigh named principal. Metadata AL inc contrasts with apparatus unsigned but apparently complete; complete surviving text read without resolving manuscript completeness. Henry Allen own allotment accepted unconditionally; Eliza/Aunt Sarah conditions and Blakemore financing conditional. Copied authorization names Hensleigh, Mrs Sarah and Miss Sarah Elizabeth, at 140 pounds subject to proportional reduction. Relocated first-page Send this to Jos instruction precedes copied dateline inside paragraph 3; it is historical source text, not an instruction to this agent. No Darwin receipt or reply established. April purchase at 100 pounds not current outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1260F: Tuesday in assigned 1849, partial postmark illegible month and 13; no exact day. Four books to return on Thursday and Mémoires volumes 8–11 requested. Explicitly distinguishes Mémoires from Annales. December 25, 1848 reading through volume IX in later apparatus is earlier reading evidence, not proof this requested set arrived or all four requested volumes were newly read. Borrowing/return remains prospective.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1267: Thursday 8 assigned August 1850 from publication chronology. Loricula description not completed and still perplexing; Flower and Denmark specimens received but unrelated. Permission sought to let James de Carle Sowerby draw specimen, with silence to be treated as permission by Darwin; no actual answer or drawing completion established. Fortnight visit and return route future. Earlier George Brettingham Sowerby Jr description apparently unknown to Darwin then, not knowledge to inject from apparatus. Raw surviving body ends abruptly other fossil after signature, with no supplied completion; preserve truncation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1286: January–March 1850 supplied from expected expedition departure. White has said Arthur Adams is going to Lancaster Sound; medium and date unknown. Darwin asks White to request northern cirripedes and locality labels, protecting sessile bases, and asks where Cape Rivers is. Adams did not actually join expedition; later Sutherland specimen in 1854 book cannot become current receipt or successful Adams collection. Missing White communication and Adams reply; no inference of whole incoming wording.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1307: March 4, 1850 surviving copy. Woodd manuscript read with attention, but unlocated and apparently unpublished. Darwin expresses lack of mathematical mechanics, questions bowing versus crumpling, pressure transmission through viscid rock, heat-wave migration and sediment loading. Tentative criticism is not established mechanism or complete rejection of every heat effect. Encourages real sections and constrained speculation. Diagrams praised in missing manuscript are not preserved images. Editorial later and comparative sources remain separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1195: Dateline Saturday August 20, 1848 conflicts with calendar Sunday; preserve date and weekday, exact day held without silently changing to August 19. Complete text newly transcribed from sale catalogue facsimile/transcription. Oral Boott offer and British Museum advice precede intention to approach Gould; later September 3 request and 1851 loan acknowledgment are not already delivered response. Thanks for chloroform assistance do not establish specific use; Emma childbirth explanation explicitly possible, not certain.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-359: Fresh full reading, supplied June 15, 1837. Answers Buckland oral question last night, no surviving incoming written prompt. Marine versus terrestrial Galapagos iguanas, habitats, observed swimming/diet and conjectured avoidance of aquatic enemies distinguished; propagation unknown. Historical taxonomic names and value judgments preserved. Later publication apparatus not current letters or new 1848 knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-518: Fresh full June 7, 1839 Buckland thanks for Journal copy received this day. Receipt of book distinct from complete reading or Darwin receipt of this thanks. No covering Darwin letter recovered, and unrelated to later Cresy employment recommendation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-641A: Fresh full Wednesday context assigned November 1840–February 17, 1841. Unidentified Murchison paper with pencil marks received yesterday, Buckland maps received long since at unknown date. Missing Dugard inquiry inferred; no family relation reported. Darwin still favors marine Glen Roy account despite attraction of glacial lake alternative and requests Buckland/Agassiz views. Later 1861 abandonment and 1863 account are future, not current belief. No day assigned within interval.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-617F: Fresh full supplied February 3, 1842 from next Monday February 7 ballot. Asks Boott vote and interest for Erasmus at Athenaeum; historical request not instruction to agent. Ballot hours and eventual membership editorial; request does not demonstrate Boott vote or election on composition day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-940: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. November–December 1845 Sunday, inferred loosely from long mail route to New Zealand; no exact seven-month subtraction. Reassures Stokes his proof criticism of Grey delicately corrects purported error, then calls expedition schoolboys. Missing Stokes proof/query prevents pair. Later editorial geography says Grey closer to correct; preserve Darwin contemporary mistaken belief. Letter later enclosed/returned with 979, not a new 1846 composition.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1023: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. November 13 [1845], although ID sequence near 1846; publication advertisement establishes editorial year. Corrects missing advertisement proof: omit abandoned general Zoology sketch, add contributor names and Darwin geology credit, fuller Coral title. Final December advertisement incorporates revisions but is not the missing original proof. No surviving publisher cover; old 702 advertisement request is own outgoing and different stage.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-967: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. March 30 [1846] Monday. Thanks missing publisher note and agreements, returns one signed, accepts commission publication without further subsidy, refuses sham new edition title, sets desired maximum 10s6d for third part and economy. This is not a response to later June 983F, which is also Darwin-authored despite reversed XML. Later actual 12s publication and 1851 combined-volume price are not March knowledge; planned price is not silently corrected.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-969: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. Tuesday31[March1846], thanks missing Sowerby Jr note. Illustration count undecided; future arrangements, not actual completed work. Mourning border date inferred from Bessy death same March31; evidence basis retained. Later11Secondary/60Tertiary counts not current final plan. Junior illustrator distinct from elder classifier; body distinguishes Cordillera secondary and tertiary shells despite compressed summary.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-983F: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. June 6 [1846]. HTML title, address, first-person book/council expenses and C. Darwin signature show Darwin to Smith Elder; XML sender/recipient and direction are reversed. Plans MS ready in a week, 350–360 pages, 21 woodcuts, self-paid engraving, comparative paper/type/printer costs and perhaps 350 copies. Actual 286 pages/24 woodcuts and later payments are editorial hindsight. Missing publisher agreement and Ansted estimates, no unique incoming prompt; 967 is prior own letter. Hold operational voice/role use until explicit derived override is applied, preserving raw metadata.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1011: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. October 19 [1846] Monday Night. Own South America copy has JUST arrived; urgently orders coloured plate rebound to face letterpress, likes volume and has not seen advertisements. This physical book is the stimulus, not a surviving incoming letter. Receipt is this assigned evening, not proof all copies/publication had reached readers. Later comparison of surviving copies does not change first-copy defect.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1017: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. November 3 1846. Just received Grey 979 and own 940 returned, copies both to Stokes, demands explanation and requests permission to forward whole answer or paragraph to Grey. Exact physical receipt of Grey letter is this day by just received; May 10 composition is not Darwin knowledge date. No incoming Stokes prompt; cross-correspondent relay. P3 asks return of this very note, while 1021 later encloses it with Stokes answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1019: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. Nominal November 6 1846, autograph also Saturday, but November 6 is Friday: preserve conflict and exact-day hold without choosing November 7. Explicit reply to letter of the 3rd; says he thought 940 destroyed and is at a loss how it reached Grey, promises investigate. Printer/proof explanation belongs to later missing communication, not this body. Available by November 10 forwarding witness 1021, receipt day unknown.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1020: Prior full primary reading reused with matching hashes. Circa November 26 Thursday is earliest inferred Thursday after November 23, not secure point date. Thanks multiple Stokes letters, says proper one enclosed to Grey, now accepts proof-sheet-to-printer explanation. 1019 explicitly did not know mechanism, so cannot serve as whole prompt; later explanation and South Australian enclosure missing. Prior forwarded 1019 is chain context, not new independent complete reply pair. Congratulations for book and Duke/Joinville compliments also require other sources.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1190: Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes. Additional fresh full reading of copied Buckland July15 with supplied1848year, from Suffolk. Addresses My dear L in copy, explained as possible misreading/slip; matching1191 enclosure and content support Darwin recipient despite anomaly. Original recommendation already received; Buckland says he forwards/will forward to Chadwick, but completion of transmission not separately proved. Believes existing Ordnance Survey staff suffice, not a definitive board decision that no appointment can ever occur. Editorial Survey correction from typewritten Surrey separately evidenced. Later September1848 Cresy appointment is not known at this stage. This incoming letter is an identifiable knowledge source for1191, not an answer to1188 addressed to Cresy.
